questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number.

19 : 441 :: 17 : ?
questions.solution:
The pattern follows here are:

***First number : (First number + 2)² = Second number***

The 1st term 19 = (19 + 2)² = (21)² = 441

Similarly,

**The 2nd term 17 = (17 + 2)² = (19)² = 361**

So, the correct option will be** 361.**

questions.question:
Select the option that will correctly replace the question mark (?) in the series.

15, 19, 35, 71, ?
questions.solution:
15 + (2)² = 19

19 + (4)² = 35

35 + (6)² = 71

71 + (8)² = 135

So, the correct option will be option 4.

questions.question:
The statements below are followed by two conclusions labeled I and II. Assuming that the information in the statements is true, even if it appears at variance with generally established facts, decide which conclusion(s) logically and definitely follow(s) from the information given in the statements.

Statements:

1) All goats are dogs.

2) Some goats are cows.

Conclusion:

I. Some dogs are cows.

II. Some cows are dogs.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor conclusion II follows.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is given below-

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3836b1df7c29518e5c3f90041d3c9315b0e4b828cb86e85750a31702cedd3ff8.png] 

Conclusion:

1) Some dogs are cows → True (Some goats are cow and all goats are dog so it is true that some dogs are cow)

2) Some cows are dogs → True (Some goats are cow and all goats are dog so it is true that some cows are dog)

So, Both Conclusion I and II follow.

questions.question:
Find out the two signs to be interchanged to make the following equation correct.

24 + 2 × 2 − 6 ÷ 3 = 22
questions.solution:
By interchanging signs + and -, we get

24 - 2 × 2 + 6 ÷ 3 = 24 – 4 + 2 = 22

So, the correct option will be option 3.
